ANC: The Big Breakup

By: Kate Barry | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The Big Breakup between the ANC and their voters means they're hooking up with other parties. But where will we be in 2024?

Unique Selling Point:
A satirical look at the fallout of the recent Municipal Elections, and what led to the low voter turnout. Story structure loosely follows the patter of an relationship breakup, citing the main issues that usually spell disaster in an intimate partnership.
The voters are looking for a partner who will provide for their basic needs: Home, Job, Water Electricity.
With the help of political analysts, a journalist, party leaders and a couples counsellor, we look at what's gone wrong and what it means for our future? Will the voters find a new partner that makes them happy, or is this a toxic relationship which the abused partner can never leave?

Summary:
1. The Promise "I Do" - despite losing votes since 2013 (nene fired, PP State of Capture Report, Nkandla Ruling, Zuma corruption charges) the people said YES.

2. The Performance: - (Bad sex, uncleanliness, laziness, weight gain, unfair division of labour)
#GuptaLeaks shocked us all, no water, no electricity, bloated salaries, theft, corruption, no action from NPA

3. The Let-Down - (Cheating, fighting about money)
Zondo Commission exposed extent of ANC corruption, looting of SOE's, Magashule corruption charges, Durban Mayor corruption charges, VBS, Covid-19 lockdown, PPE corruption, Digital Vibes saga

4. The Big Blow-Up - Zuma contempt of Curt, Zuma imprisonment, July riots resulting in fear, disillusionment, gatvolness, emigration.

5. The Break- Up - 2021 Elections. Low voter turnout (ghosting), Shock loss of majority in KZN (found someone else), more attractive choices - ActionSA, Patriotic Alliance, EFF, VVF+ (Tinder/Grindr - swipe left on ANC, swipe right on new kid
Guilt and blame - therapy for Ungeni councillors who lost their jobs

6. The Make-Up - Will Ramaphosa survive 2022 ANC Electoral Conference? Who is the alternative? (DD Mabuza, Paul Mashatile, Lindiwe Sisulu?)

7. 2024 General Election
If ANC doesn't get 50% majorly who will be the coalition partner?
EFF - Worst nightmare for progressive democrats
DA & others - Swingers party

Script:


THE BIG BREAKUP

V/O: The local government elections have come and gone, and with less than 50% of the vote the ANC is feeling the sting of rejection. So what does the future hold for a party that no longer sets hearts on fire?

Dawie: If you look at a classic example of an ANC stronghold, a place like Soweto in the city of Johannesburg, turnout was 41%, so it just implies that a huge amount of former ANC voters didn’t go vote in this election.

V/O; Dawie Scholtz is an independent elections analyst who developed a statistical model to crunch the numbers.

Dawie: In 2011 the ANC won 86% in Soweto. So this year they won 53% in Soweto. So not only did most voters stay away, but of those voters that did go vote ANC suffered massive losses in its core support base. Huge surprise.

Link: The romance between the ANC and their supporters has been the stuff of fairy-tales, and despite their ups and downs over the years, nothing could come between the party and the people. For better or worse, they always gave them another chance because they’d said: I do.

V/O: So what could be the reason for this big breakup? Long before the 2016 Elections the red flags were billowing: the firing of Finance Minister Nhanhla Nene that sent markets plummeting, the Public Protector’s State of Capture Report into corruption, The Constitutional Court ruling on Nkandla that found that President Zuma had violated his Oath of Office. The promise had been broken.

Dr Eve: The red flags are there, but I choose not to see them because he is my hero, right?

V/O: Now we know it’s a little crazy, but who better to give advice about a relationship on the rocks than a relationship expert like Dr Eve?

Dr Eve: And then it’s actually you’re not offering those basic things that I need – the safety and security. And then you begin to question and the conflict begins to happen. We begin to feel unseen, unheard. There isn’t any sense of attachment and intimacy that exists any longer.
And the moment that we bring in a third person, well that’s when things really become different. I didn’t know that I couldn’t trust you with money! I didn’t know that I couldn’t trust you with familiarity, with you bringing in new people. You bring in a new family!

V/O: With the release of the #Gupta Leaks the ANC suffered a major dent in its credibility. The media broke story after story of the extent of the Gupta family’s looting of State coffers.

Mcebisi: Jacob Zuma disfigured the ANC in a way and made it his own ANC, into a neo-patrimonial party where state power is used for personal interest.

V/O: And this trend has trickled down, according to Professor Mcebisi Ndletyana a political scientist at the University of Johannesburg.

Mcebisi: Local government has been deteriorating. In fact, if you look at the Auditor General’s Report they are saying they are worse now than they were in 2016.
Added to that the testimonies of the Zondo Commission.

V/O: For 3 years the Zondo Commission of Inquiry into State Capture heard witness after witness exposing the depth and breadth of corruption; how almost every state-owned enterprise was deliberately hollowed out and rendered ineffective, so that it could be looted. It’s estimated that over R500 billion was stolen from South Africa during the Zuma years.

Link: It was only when the rumours and reports of corruption were confirmed by witnesses at the Commission and in the Courts that the voters could no longer look away. This was the big let-down, the breach of trust, the unforgiveable infidelity.

Dr Eve: There has to be commitment, really important. Commitment means reliability and predictability. It has to be trust, and it has to be respect and honesty. And if you don’t have those 4, you’re not going to stay in love. A table of 4 loses a leg of commitment, of trust, respect, passion, and the relationship is going to fall away.

V/O: Making things even more difficult was the Covid-19 pandemic. The cycle of hard lockdowns meant the loss of thousands of jobs and the misery of being forced to stay at home by the police and the army. But then, to add insult to injury, came news of R13 billion rand in PPE tender fraud. On top of that the Digital Vibes saga involving then Minister of Health Zweli Mkhize and his family.

Mcebisi: Honestly! I mean theft of money for people who are dying! Who steals money intended for people that are dying? So you know disgusting acts like that, they’ve created a bit of doubt over whether or not the president has authority to enforce what he preaches.

Richard: It’s a party that has really lost its way and appears broken beyond redemption. They are going to have to work extremely hard to recover lost ground, to rehabilitate the broken trust of the people.

V/O: Richard Calland is an Associate Professor in Public Law at UCT.

Richard: What matters is stable government. That’s what the country needs. It’s what residents of cities need.

V/O: In July came the Big Blow-Up. When Jacob Zuma was convicted and sent to prison for contempt of court, his supporters rioted. Violence and looting engulfed KwaZulu Natal and parts of Gauteng, leaving 337 people dead and hundreds of farms and businesses destroyed. The police seemed unable or unwilling to intervene.

Richard: I think that's where we can be very clear now that burning down one and a half provinces is not a good election campaign strategy. It happened on the ANC’s watch at both national and provincial level, and so therefore inevitably the public was bound to kick back against that.

Dawie: The numbers in KZN are truly shocking for the ANC. You know, they lost like upwards of 15 to 20% of their vote in their core areas in KZN which is just unheard of. Like many, many people stayed away. So something went wrong there.

Mcebisi: In KZN that Zuma factor – ANC turning against each other, inciting civil unrest - has disfigured the image of the ANC amongst the locals. And that is why the IFP, the old, conservative, orderly folks, because KZN politics – because of the saliency of ethnic values, ethnicity, so conservativeness, respect for the law and order are key things.

Richard: No doubt they’ve got a KZN problem, and within that of course they’ve got a Zuma problem. And the failure of the ANC to tackle Jacob Zuma and his determination of him and his followers to destabilize the ANC, destabilize the country and its economy has really cost the ANC as well as the country dearly.

Mcebisi And voters have realized that this is what these folks have become. It’s not a mistake. They’re not coming back.

Bongani: The ANC doesn’t bring us flowers anymore?

Mcebisi: And memories have faded. Romance has gone out. So voters are like: What have you done for me lately?

Link: The 1st of November wasn’t just Election Day: it was the day of the Big Break-up. This was the day the ANC supporters ghosted the party. And they didn’t make a big scene – they simply walked away.

Richard: The real story here was the ANC voters saying: We are tired of you, you’ve messed us around. You lied to us, you cheated on us, but we don’t yet trust the others enough to move to them.

V/O: Only 3 out of 10 eligible voters actually voted. With no clear majority in 66 hung councils around the country, parties will be forced to work together.

Richard: You really don't want to get into bed with someone who is going to treat you badly and who is going - to put it to put it very bluntly - screw you. You need to be in bed with somebody who you can form a stable relationship with, and you can develop your own brand, build respect with the electorate, regardless of the other party.

V/O: The ANC may have lost its appeal, but so it seems did the DA. The voters showed more interest in the smaller parties – and one of the big winners of the election in Gauteng is newcomer Action SA, led by the former Mayor of Johannesburg Herman Mashaba.

Dawie: A good result you know, they got 20% of the vote in Soweto. That’s enormous. And I was just doing the analysis this morning – they also happened to get 20% in Sandton. So I think it’s the first time ever there’s a party that does relatively well in both Sandton and Soweto. And someone tweeted at me that’s the first time I’ve ever seen Sandton and Soweto has agreed on something.

V/O: Cyril Ramaphosa might be more popular than his party, but can the ANC win back lost lovers in time for the General Election in 2024?

Richard: That’s not a foregone conclusion anymore. The ANC is beatable. That is very clear now.

V/O: In response the ANC said it’s heard the voters loud and clear and promises to act with urgency to improve its performance.

Mcebisi: They’ll have to work hard. So they’ll have to sleep out in the couch for quite some time, out in the cold. Repeatedly behave well to earn back that trust. So it might take a while.
